title: CmdPal: Palette opened from Dock has an offset

judgment.rationale: The palette-offset report is already bounded by a screenshot, a direct Dock repro, and current code that still applies a hardcoded padding offset after computing the launch anchor.
evidence: The issue includes a screenshot showing the Command Palette window separated from the dock item that opened it.
Current source in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockWindow.xaml.cs still sets paddingDips = 8 and then shifts the launch position away from the dock before sending ShowPaletteAtMessage.
The issue is scoped to a dev build and a very specific visual geometry symptom rather than a broad Dock failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused Dock anchoring design, after maintainer-side repro, that removes or conditions the hardcoded gap between the dock trigger and the launched palette.

fix_assessment.rationale: A small repository change in Dock launch anchoring is likely enough, but maintainer-side repro should confirm whether the full 8-DIP offset is always incorrect or only wrong for certain dock positions.

issue_context.summary: A collaborator reports that the Command Palette window opens with a visible gap from the dock item that launched it, especially from the center dock band.
known_information: The issue is filed against a dev build on main, not a stale released build.
The screenshot shows a consistent visual gap rather than a random placement failure.
The issue specifically expects the palette to align with the dock item that opened it.
inferences: This is a small geometry bug in Dock-to-palette anchoring rather than a monitor-topology or focus-management issue.
The hardcoded offset in DockWindow is more likely than not the user-visible gap, but maintainers should confirm whether any shadow-padding behavior also depends on that value.
issue_context.analysis: This is one of the stronger lightweight actionable-design cases in the batch. The issue is narrow, the screenshot is concrete, and the current code still contains a hardcoded launch offset applied immediately before the palette is shown. That is enough to propose a focused fix direction while still pairing it with a reproduce action because the precise acceptable gap may depend on palette shadow/card geometry.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockWindow.xaml.cs computes the dock-side anchor and then applies paddingDips = 8 before sending ShowPaletteAtMessage.
git blame shows the 8-DIP offset originates from the original Dock implementation rather than a later targeted fix for this issue, so the current geometry still matches the reported symptom.

actions.label: Reproduce Dock palette launch offset

prerequisites: Place at least one clickable band in the center dock area.
steps: Open the dock and click an item that launches the main Command Palette window.
Observe the first opened palette position relative to the clicked dock item.
Repeat from another dock side if available to see whether the visible gap is tied to one side or is universal.
reproduce.expected_result: The visible Command Palette card should align with the dock trigger instead of opening with an extra detached gap.

actions.note: Maintainer-side local repro guidance only; this artifact does not post upstream content.

actions.label: Approve Dock palette alignment design
actions.note: Dashboard-only action. No upstream comment or PR is posted by this artifact update.

proposed_fixes.title: Anchor the palette to the dock trigger instead of always adding an 8-DIP gap
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DockWindow.RequestShowPaletteOnUiThread computes the correct anchor side and then unconditionally pushes the launched palette 8 DIPs away from the dock, which produces the visible gap shown in the issue.
plan: Trace how the dock click position becomes screenPosPixels and separate shadow/card padding concerns from the actual anchor point used to launch the palette.
Remove or condition the hardcoded 8-DIP offset so the palette aligns with the dock item or visible dock edge instead of appearing detached.
Add a focused Dock launch regression check for center-band and side-dock placements so the geometry change does not break multi-position anchoring.
verification: Open the palette from a center dock band and confirm the visible card aligns with the triggering dock item instead of floating below or beside it.
Repeat from top, bottom, left, and right dock positions and confirm the palette still opens on the correct side without clipping.

confidence.rationale: The screenshot and current hardcoded padding make the likely cause strong, but a quick maintainer-side repro should confirm whether any shadow-spacing requirement still justifies a smaller conditional offset.
